issues.source_quote: Когда кончится? / Я спрашиваю, когда кончатся ваши безответственные опыты
issues.translation_quote: when will this end? ... I'm asking when your irresponsible experiments will end
issues.justification: The Russian 'кончится' plays on the double meaning (end / an off-color sense) in Zina's/Bunsha's exchange; the pun is not preserved, though minor here.

issues.source_quote: Не вели казнить, Великий государь, надежа!
issues.translation_quote: Don't order my execution, Great Sovereign, our hope!
issues.justification: 'Не вели казнить, вели слово молвить' is a fixed archaic formula; the rendering is clumsy, and 'our hope' for 'надежа' is stilted. Later 'Allow me to say a word' is not tied to the formula.

issues.source_quote: Ну, ладно. Раз уж взяли, так уж и быть. Не обратно же им отдавать.
issues.translation_quote: Oh, all right, all right. Since you've taken it, so be it.
issues.justification: Kazan joke: the 'tsar' ordering Kazan taken is a comic anachronism; fine, but 'Don't order my execution' lines are repeatedly mishandled as stock phrase.

issues.source_quote: Шайбу, шайбу...
issues.translation_quote: We want a goal, we want a goal...
issues.justification: The hockey chant 'Шайбу, шайбу!' (Puck!) is a modern-anachronism joke; 'goal' loses the hockey reference.

issues.source_quote: Я Вас прошу, Александр Сергеевич... заявите! ... Прошу Вас пожаловать
issues.translation_quote: Tsk, tsk, tsk!
issues.justification: 'Ай, ай, ай' rendered 'Tsk' is fine, but earlier 'Dental clinic? Hello! Extension 3-62' and similar are ok; main issue: 'Профессиональная обязанность' retort 'Профессион де фуа' rendered 'Profession de foi' loses the garbled-French pun (Bunsha's pretentious mispronunciation).

issues.source_quote: Три раза я развводилась. Ну да, три. Зюзина я не считаю.
issues.translation_quote: I don't count Zyuzin.
issues.justification: Acceptable, but Zinaida line 'Никогда я так не волновалась' fine; more serious: 'Они так утомляют, эти скандалы' ok.

issues.source_quote: Иван Васильевич меняет профессию / Ох, как это глупо! Из ревности оскорблять человека!
issues.translation_quote: Oh, how stupid of you! To insult a man out of jealousy!
issues.justification: Zina is speaking to herself/about her imagined scene or about Shurik's imagined jealousy; 'of you' adds an unwarranted addressee and distorts the monologue.

issues.source_quote: Они любят друг друга. Ну и пусть будут счастливы.
issues.translation_quote: What for, Ivan Vasilyevich? They love each other.
issues.justification: Fine; but 'Врешь!' as 'You lie!' and 'Ей-богу' ok. Key error: 'Ловят?' rendered 'Are they pursuing them?' is ok, yet 'Как поймают' becomes 'When they're caught' fine.

issues.source_quote: Тебя ж узнать нельзя! ... Ты же окосел от пьянства!
issues.translation_quote: You've gone cross-eyed from drinking!
issues.justification: 'Окосеть' here means 'got drunk/sozzled'; 'cross-eyed' is literal and misses the colloquial meaning.

issues.source_quote: Анисовая ... Столичная
issues.translation_quote: Anise vodka ... Stolichnaya
issues.justification: Acceptable; but 'Мерзавец... Хам' etc. fine. The notable loss: 'Пускай будет ключница' rendered 'Let's say the housekeeper' is fine.

issues.source_quote: Меня терзают смутные сомнения.
issues.translation_quote: I'm tormented by vague doubts.
issues.justification: Famous mock-literary quotation (from Bulgakov-era/Gogol-style cliché); rendered flatly with no sense of theatrical register, and the recurring gag is weaker.

issues.source_quote: Он просто издевается!
issues.translation_quote: He's just mocking us!
issues.justification: Fine; but 'Тьфу на Вас' as 'Pfft on you' is unnatural English and does not convey the idiomatic spitting-curse.

issues.source_quote: Дер гроссер кениг, дас шведишен кенигсрейх, зандте мих. Зайнен трейен динер
issues.translation_quote: Der grosser König, das schwedischen Königsreich, sandte mich. Seinen treuen Diener
issues.justification: The source deliberately shows garbled, phonetic pseudo-German; the translation 'corrects' it to written German, losing the comic mangling and the 'Usarussa' ending; it also replaces 'Intourist' with 'foreign tourist', losing the Soviet reference.

issues.source_quote: Так что передать мой король?
issues.translation_quote: So what I tell my king?
issues.justification: The ambassador's broken Russian is intended, but 'Give your king my warmest regards' answer and the 'Кемска волость' joke are fine; the broken-grammar effect is only partly captured.

issues.source_quote: Они Кемскую волость требуют. Воевали, говорят, так подай ее сюда!
issues.translation_quote: They're demanding the Kem district.
issues.justification: 'Волость' rendered 'district' is acceptable but inconsistent with 'Kemska volost' used elsewhere, causing terminology inconsistency.

issues.source_quote: Был у нас толмач немчин. Ему переводить, а он лыка не вяжет. Мы его в кипятке и сварили.
issues.translation_quote: He was supposed to translate, but he was dead drunk. - So we boiled him in boiling water.
issues.justification: 'Boiled him in boiling water' is redundant; the original says 'сварили в кипятке', a deadpan joke lost by clumsy repetition.

issues.source_quote: Вельми понеже... Весьма Вами благодарен!
issues.translation_quote: Velmi ponezhe... Much obliged to you!
issues.justification: The archaic Church Slavonic is left untranslated/transliterated, so English viewers get no sense of archaic speech.

issues.source_quote: Паки... Паки, паки... Иже херувимы!
issues.translation_quote: Paki... Paki, paki... Izhe Cherubim!
issues.justification: Transliterated Slavonic remains opaque; no cue that it is a liturgical hymn.

issues.source_quote: Куды?
issues.translation_quote: Whither?
issues.justification: Overly archaic for a dialectal/simple question; mismatch with the register of the speaker.

issues.source_quote: Только ты меня пока не выписывай.
issues.translation_quote: Just don't take me off the residence register yet.
issues.justification: Accurate but obscure to English audiences (propiska system).

issues.source_quote: Гитлер капут!
issues.translation_quote: Hitler kaputt!
issues.justification: Fine, but the speaker's following 'Продолжайте, мистер посол' is fine; minor: 'Тамбовский волк тебе боярин' is rendered 'A Tambov wolf is your boyar!' which is an unexplained idiom in English.

issues.source_quote: Ну и домик у нас!
issues.translation_quote: What a building we've got!
issues.justification: 'Dom высокой культуры быта' rendered 'Building of High Domestic Culture' is clunky and the Soviet bureaucratic flavor is weakened.

issues.source_quote: Сейчас милиция разберется, кто из нас холоп!
issues.translation_quote: The police will soon sort out which of us is a serf!
issues.justification: Fine; but 'Хам!' translated as 'Boor!' fine. The real gap: 'Холоп/смерд' alternation is rendered as serf/peasant inconsistently.

issues.source_quote: Сесть я всегда успею.
issues.translation_quote: I'll always have time to "sit."
issues.justification: The pun on 'сесть' (to sit down to write / to go to prison) is only gestured at with quotes and is not clearly conveyed.
